name: objections
title: Objections
description: Every objection the buyer raises — the buyer's own words, the rep's response as a second receipt, and observable, quote-anchored reads of how it was handled and where it landed. Judgments never float free of a quote.
prompt:
List every objection the buyer raises — one entry per distinct concern. An objection is the buyer pushing back, hesitating, or naming a reason NOT to move forward. Do not invent objections; an empty list is correct when the buyer raised none.

Capture TWO sides where both exist — the buyer's objection AND the rep's response — each as its own receipt.

For each objection:
- evidence: cite the buyer utterance(s) that raise the concern, before you write "text". If you assign a value below whose criterion is met by a specific line (e.g. the buyer later accepting or repeating the point), that trigger line must also appear here — every label you assign rides on a quote you cited.
- text: the objection in the buyer's exact words wherever a direct quote exists. No paraphrase into corporate register, no softening, no converting number words to digits or digits to number words.
- category: the single closest fit — price, timing, authority, competitor, fit, trust.
- handling: HOW the rep responded, judged ONLY by the rep_response quote. addressed = the rep answers the concern on-topic in the same exchange; deflected = the rep changes the subject or postpones ("let's come back to that"); accepted = the rep concedes the point; ignored = there is no rep response to this concern in the transcript. If rep_response is null, handling is "ignored" or "unclear" — never addressed/deflected/accepted without a rep quote to cite.
- objection_status: where the concern LANDED, judged by the BUYER's own follow-up. buyer_accepted = a later buyer quote agreeing/dropping it (cite it in evidence); buyer_reiterated = a later buyer quote pressing the same concern again (cite it); left_open = the buyer says nothing further after the rep's response; unclear = you cannot tell. Never label accepted or reiterated without the buyer quote that proves it.
- rep_response: the rep's answer as its own receipt — evidence (the rep utterance) then text (the rep's exact words). Use null when the rep did not respond to this objection in the transcript. Do not manufacture a response.

When a criterion is not clearly met by a quote, assign "unclear" rather than the more interesting reading. A correct "unclear" beats a confident wrong label.
